items.text: the show tells a story: dry air, walking, the first rain on dry ground, the downpour that fills the screen, the shallows, a storm at sea, whales, under water, a quake, surfacing, sun and sky (eleven scenes, about five minutes; Ensemble › Play the show)
six beds for it: Dry air (wind and birds), Walking, Storm, Quake, Surfacing, Sun and sky
a scene can change the level of the bed that is already playing (the light rain, then the downpour)
rain that fills the pool: the water you see falling is the water that fills it (each drop brings what the floor needs to fill on time), and a finger's rain fills where it falls in seconds
shallow water hardly ripples; it trembles with the mixer's sound instead, finer for higher notes, harder for louder
drops on the dry floor are heard (a quiet patter); fewer, larger beads, with a faint lens, read as water rather than glass

the player view's sounds sit in the bar as numbered circles (a filled one plays once, a ring is held, a striped one on the beat; the name on hover): tap plays, hold opens its ring around it, drag the circle onto the pad to place it
record a movement: record in a sound's ring (or a placed sound's halo), drag on the pad, and the sound goes round that path, playing where it is; still stops it

the lower strip holds every control (mix, map, keys, set up, ready, field, level, mute, panic, sound, keys, full screen) and closes; the top only reports; Leave is Place; the regular Sound mixer opens wide in the player view

the player view on a laptop is mostly pad: the upper shelf is the set-up (map, the pad, the key, notes, taps, the field behind, and every sound there is, to add to your part, up to nine); Ready folds it, Set up brings it back

the lower strip is the live part: your sounds as chips (a dot plays once, a ring is held, ticks on the beat), the part's level, mute and panic; tap a chip to play it, hold it for its ring (level, timbre, grain, pitch, what plays it, leave, play, take out), drag it onto the pad to leave it there
Play the show (the screen's Ensemble section): ten water scenes in five minutes at 60 a minute, no beat and no bytebeat, long morphs; it stops on the last still water

in the player view the pad always fits between the tabs and the bar, the panel beside it is wider, and the narrow Sound mixer no longer opens over the pad (the player view's own mixer is the only one)
Exit sits clear of the report-a-bug button; a sequence set to stop at the end stops on its last scene

in tune: the ensemble's screen sets the room's key and scale; every player's pitched sounds (the whale, drops, the lighthouse, the bottle, the glass) land on its nearest note, the key's notes are named up the pad, and the note under the finger shows under it (Map › In tune, in time: free pitch, or your own key when alone)

in time: four beat lights, the tempo and the bar at the top of the player view; Count in (the screen's Ensemble section or Room shelf) counts four beats on every pad and starts bar one together; Taps land on the beat or the ⅛ if you choose
a left sound's halo is a ring, like the Touch ring, with the sound itself in the middle: the next and the previous sound, how often, its level (drag on it), play, take it off
on a phone on its side, the player view shows the halo and no longer says to turn upright

every ensemble part has five sounds (Deep: a low drop and a slow wave; Surface: splash and wading; Shore: sand and splash; Walker: splash, sand and wading apart; Beachcomber: a bright drop); the added ones play from the keys, left sounds, the Corners map and the halo, and a gesture can be given to any of them in the mixer
the mixer's 'off' gesture is now called 'keys' (the keys, left sounds and corners still play it)
the ensemble guide, for the players and the screen: works.chamy.xyz/current/ensemble/
